item.title: Who was Yasser Abu Shabab? Israel-backed anti-Hamas militia leader killed in Gaza
item.description: A prominent anti-Hamas militia leader, Yasser Abu Shabab, was killed in an internal clash in southern Gaza. He was reportedly taken to an Israeli hospital where he died. The incident highlights ongoing internal conflicts within anti-Hamas groups operating in Gaza amidst broader Israeli military operations against Hamas operatives.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Grand jury rejects justice department's bid to revive criminal case against New York Attorney General Letitia James
item.description: A federal grand jury rejected prosecutors' attempt to revive criminal charges against New York Attorney General Letitia James. This decision follows a judge's earlier dismissal of the indictment, citing the unlawful appointment of the prosecutor. Prosecutors intend to seek a new indictment, marking the Justice Department's second effort to prosecute James.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: US Supreme Court lets Texas use new Congressional map, boosting GOP ahead of 2026 midterms
item.description: The US Supreme Court has allowed Texas to implement its new congressional map, potentially securing five extra House seats for Republicans in 2026. This decision overturns a lower court's block over racial discrimination allegations.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Traveller who visited every country says North Korea nearly put him in prison after friend scattered ashes
item.description: Danish traveller Henrik Jeppesen, who has visited every country on Earth, says North Korea was the only place where he genuinely feared prison. His companion secretly scattered a friend’s ashes at the DMZ despite guides refusing permission, then filmed it. When airport officials found the video, both men were accused of “polluting” the country and escaped only after an apology letter.
item.dc:creator: TOI Trending Desk

item.title: HasanAbi blasts Asmongold, Ethan Klein, Destiny for hyping “Free Kaya” sniper
item.description: Streamer Hasan Piker faced a fan protest during a live broadcast, prompting him to accuse fellow creators like Asmongold, Ethan Klein, and Destiny of normalizing harassment. Piker argued that celebrating real-world confrontations, even over past controversies like the 'Free Kaya' incident, fuels dangerous fan behavior and blurs lines between content and endangerment.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Jack the Ripper solved? DNA on a shawl points to a Polish 19th-century immigrant; experts say it can’t be
item.description: A new claim about Jack the Ripper’s identity has resurfaced, this time hinging on disputed DNA from a shawl allegedly found at an 1888 crime scene. Russell Edwards says it proves Polish immigrant Aaron Kosminski was the killer, but forensic experts dismiss the evidence as weak, contaminated and statistically meaningless. More than a century on, the Ripper remains unsolved, fuelled by speculation rather than certainty.

item.title: What’s behind the “Free Kaya” slogan that crashed HasanAbi’s livestream?
item.description: Hasan Piker, known as HasanAbi, faced a public protest during his Ireland stream. A masked individual shouted 'Free Kaya,' referencing a past controversy involving his dog. This incident demonstrates how online disputes can manifest in real life, with 'Free Kaya' becoming a symbol of viewer concerns about animal welfare among streamers.

item.title: RaKai breaks silence on Walmart flower incident that led to Twitch ban
item.description: Controversial streamer RaKai faced a Twitch suspension after a viral Walmart clip showed him handing flowers to a woman without apparent payment. He claims it was a mistake, with an assistant instructed to return the unpaid bouquet. Twitch initially cited a two-year ban for illegal activities, later clarifying it was a display bug, though his reputation is impacted.

item.title: Nike shoes, hoodie, and a black bag: Inside the 5-year manhunt for Jan. 6 bomb suspect Brian Cole
item.description: In a dramatic turn of events, federal agents captured Brian Cole in Virginia after a five-year manhunt. He stands accused of placing pipe bombs near the DNC and RNC offices just before the Capitol riot on January 6th.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Pakistan reshapes defence: Asim Munir becomes first Chief of Defence Forces; President Zardari approves historic appointment
item.description: President Zardari appointed Army Chief Asim Munir as Pakistan's first Chief of Defence Forces for five years, following the 27th Constitutional Amendment. This new role unifies command across the armed forces, replacing the abolished CJCSC. Munir now holds a dual position as COAS and CDF, a significant shift in military hierarchy.

item.title: Khaleda Zia to be flown to London: Air ambulance approved for critically ill ex-Bangladesh PM; transfer likely by Friday
item.description: Former Bangladesh Prime Minister Khaleda Zia will be transferred to London for specialist treatment due to a chest infection affecting her heart and lungs. An expanded medical board, including international specialists, unanimously decided on the air ambulance transfer. Zia, 80, has been hospitalized since November 23 and moved to the CCU due to deteriorating health.

item.title: Physicists prove universe cannot be a simulation: New study debunks simulation hypothesis
item.description: Scientists at the University of British Columbia Okanagan say they’ve found a mathematical limit that shuts down the Simulation Hypothesis entirely. Drawing on Gödel’s incompleteness theorem, their study argues that parts of reality cannot be generated by any algorithm, which means no computer, however advanced, could ever build a universe like ours. The obstacle isn’t processing power. It’s logic itself.

item.title: “Just got this house”: Inside the strange burglary that hit Marlon Gracia’s home while he was streaming across the country
item.description: Twitch streamer Marlon Lundgren Garcia returned from a 40-day IRL marathon to find his recently purchased home broken into, with a smashed back door, scattered belongings, and several valuables stolen, including his PS5. He shared videos on X and Snapchat showing the damage and investigation. The incident follows his June 2025 assault, raising renewed concerns about his safety.
